findings.note: usage_verbs (cli_version.rs:355-380) treats every lowercase token of any two-space-indented line as a verb until a non-verb token, so a description line laid out differently is scraped as verbs. Same unreliable-oracle defect as G1. Latent today: the wrapped line at main.rs:55 starts with a run of spaces, so it yields an empty column.

cli_version.rs:391 uses a bare starts_with("usage: req {command}") while its twin at :442-444 requires a whitespace boundary, and the comment at :435-436 claims a with-corpus case that the NoCorpus fixture does not exercise.

cli_version.rs:486-490 asserts that trace's page 'says an undecided claim is shown in its own section', but TRACE_HELP has no such section (the reviewed commit a623e97 says exactly that). The check passes only because 'undecided' appears in the edge sentence.
Help winning over other arguments is the specified behaviour (spec R2: any --help/-h argument prints the page), so init --root --help answering the page is correct.

CANON_HELP (main.rs:241-251) lists the schema-mismatch exit 3 only under --verify, while AGENTS.md:133-139 says plain canon also exits 3 on it. The page is incomplete, but it says it is a map that points to AGENTS.md.
help_requested scanning every argument (main.rs:106-108) is the behaviour spec R2 requires (the same point as the known-false item), not a defect.
True that every test passes --help as the first or only argument (cli_version.rs:335,402), so 'help anywhere wins' is not pinned; a useful extra case, not a defect in the change.

verbs.len() >= ALL_COMMANDS.len() (cli_version.rs:515-516) is vacuous if ALL_COMMANDS is emptied. True, but that edit is unrealistic. G2's one-directional check is a different defect, and this finding's proposed fix does not address it.
